correctness.rationale: The Pauli-to-Bloch reduction gives the 3×3 real generator A and exact characteristic cubic lambda³+2lambda²+(1+u)lambda+uz. For u≤1/4, sign comparison at the z=1 slow real root shows strict global optimality. For 1/4<u<1/3, shifting lambda→x-2/3 gives x³-3s²x+b; splitting its three-real/one-real regimes proves max Re x≥s with equality only b=2s³ (EP2). For u≥1/3, trace=-2 forces max Re lambda≥-2/3, saturated uniquely at b=0 with real root 0 of depressed cubic; at u=1/3 the order-3 nilpotence proves EP3. Formula feasibility and boundary agreement checked. Independent symbolic characteristic, exact EP3 nilpotence and 8×101 finite angle comparisons passed; finite grid supports but does not prove global optimization.
residual_risks: Only fixed omega,Gamma>0, time-independent Hermitian Pauli jump and spectral exponential rate; not finite-time channel optimization.

evidence: Am-Shallem, Kosloff and Moiseyev calculate the optical Bloch EP2 curve and EP3 cusp under detuning/drive variation. Their generator uses potentially distinct T1/T2 and their criterion is EP-based parameter estimation, not our fixed-u minmax over the orientation of one Hermitian jump. General trace averaging gives the high-drive upper bound but not its threshold, uniqueness or middle EP2 optimizer.
Am-Shallem et al. already have EP3 and EP2-curve mathematics, not credited anew.

final_claim: For one qubit with fixed omega,Gamma>0 and one rotated Hermitian dephasing axis, the optimized normalized spectral gap is (1-sqrt(1-4u))/2 for u≤1/4, 2/3-sqrt((1/3-u)/3) for 1/4≤u≤1/3, and 2/3 for u≥1/3, u=(omega/Gamma)^2, with the unique explicit optimizing z=sin²theta in every branch.
